title: Using Trees as a Natural Weather Station for Wind Pattern Forecasting Applied to Forest Firefighting
content: With the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, there is a growing need to develop innovative and accessible methods for environmental monitoring. This work presents a solution based on natural trees equipped with a low-cost embedded system. The innovative idea is that measuring only internal temperature of a tree around its trunk, it is possible to evaluate some weather parameters, such as wind speed and direction. To evaluate this relationship, a multiscale decomposition technique (Discrete Wavelet Transform) and machine learning models (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM, and Linear Regression) were applied. Among the models tested, Random Forest achieved the best results, demonstrating high accuracy with an error of 6.60%. As an important outcome, the result shows that the proposed tree-based solution is viable for weather monitoring in hard-to-reach places, particularly in the context of forest fire prevention.
